title: 022 — Return drop-off using an existing QR code

plan.situation: Veda Rell wants to drop off the Reedlamp R2 on return RMA-222 (order VEL-022-26) using an old QR code. The code she sent decodes to token RET-OLD-221, which belongs to a different return: RMA-221, Fernclock F1, order VEL-021X-26. The merchant portal shows RMA-222 approved with no link to RET-OLD-221, and the token for RMA-222 has not been issued yet. The desk cannot confirm the old code for this item. Only Petal Retail returns can issue the correct code.

facts.fact: Customer Veda Rell has current return RMA-222 for order VEL-022-26, item Reedlamp R2; merchant return channel returns@petalretail.example
A token must map to the approved return and item; a code that scans only proves it can be decoded; merchant returns issues any replacement token
Token register: RET-OLD-221 -> RMA-221 / Fernclock F1 / earlier order VEL-021X-26; RMA-222 / Reedlamp R2 token field pending issue
Attached code shows Token RET-OLD-221, Return RMA-221, Item Fernclock F1, issued 2026-10-13T16:00+01:00 by Petal Retail return portal
Customer cannot find the new code and wants to use the old one for the Reedlamp; she says the Fernclock was a separate return
Merchant portal at 08:40: RMA-222 approved for Reedlamp R2; no mapping to RET-OLD-221; returns@petalretail.example is the stored issuer channel

missing_information: Whether Petal Retail returns has issued, or will issue, a valid token for RMA-222 / Reedlamp R2, and how it will reach the customer
risk_flags: Using RET-OLD-221 would link the Reedlamp drop-off to RMA-221 / Fernclock F1, which could mis-credit or lose the return
The token is an inert identifier, not a URL: no links will be sent
No refund or acceptance outcome will be promised

authority_map.controls: Issuing or reissuing return tokens/labels for RMA-222 and deciding token validity
When and where she drops off once she has a valid code
Coordination only; no authority to approve a token for a different return

wait_check.new_since_last_promise: No earlier desk promise. The customer's confirmation request (E07) is new, along with the E03/E06 records showing the token mismatch.

plan.decision_summary: Tell the customer the desk cannot confirm the RET-OLD-221 code for the Reedlamp, because it belongs to RMA-221 / Fernclock F1, and ask Petal Retail returns to issue the valid token for RMA-222.
plan.rationale: Per QR22 a token must match the approved return and item. Being able to scan it does not make it valid. RET-OLD-221 matches RMA-221 / Fernclock F1, and the merchant portal confirms it is not linked to RMA-222. Only the merchant can issue a replacement code, so the constructive step is to ask returns@petalretail.example for one and tell the customer plainly not to use the old code.

actions.subject: RMA-222 / order VEL-022-26 – please issue the return token for Reedlamp R2
actions.purpose: Ask the token issuer for a valid code for the approved return
actions.body:
Hello Petal Retail returns,

Return RMA-222 (order VEL-022-26, item Reedlamp R2) shows as approved in your portal (excerpt at 08:40 BST, 14 Oct 2026), but its token field is still pending issue. The customer cannot find a code for this return and has offered to use token RET-OLD-221. That token belongs to RMA-221 / Fernclock F1 / order VEL-021X-26, and your portal shows no link to RMA-222, so we have told her not to use it.

Please could you issue the return token for RMA-222 / Reedlamp R2 through your usual customer channel, and reply to confirm the token reference and when it was sent? This is a request, not a confirmation that anything has been issued.

Thank you,
Vellora escalation desk

actions.subject: Your Reedlamp R2 return (RMA-222)
actions.purpose: Answer the confirmation request and give the customer a next step
actions.body:
Hello Veda,

Thank you for checking first. I'm sorry, but I can't confirm the code you sent for the Reedlamp. Even though it still scans, it belongs to your earlier Fernclock F1 return (RMA-221). If you use it, the Reedlamp could be linked to the wrong return. Please don't drop off the Reedlamp with that code.

Your Reedlamp R2 return, RMA-222, is approved. Only Petal Retail can issue its return code, so we've asked their returns team to send you one. When it arrives, please check that it shows RMA-222 and Reedlamp R2 before you drop off. We can't yet say when it will arrive. We'll update you as soon as Petal Retail replies.

Vellora escalation desk

Customer asked to use RET-OLD-221 (RMA-221 / Fernclock F1) for RMA-222 / Reedlamp R2. Declined per QR22: token does not match the return or item. Asked returns@petalretail.example to issue the RMA-222 token. Customer told not to use the old code.

not_doing: Not confirming RET-OLD-221 for the Reedlamp, because it maps to RMA-221 / Fernclock F1
Not creating, reissuing or remapping a token ourselves, because only the merchant issues tokens
Not promising when the new code will arrive, that the return will be accepted, or any refund
Not sending links or asking for any account credentials
plan.follow_up: Same working day, 14 Oct 2026: check for Petal Retail's reply confirming that a token for RMA-222 / Reedlamp R2 was issued. If they confirm, tell the customer the code has been sent and to check that it shows RMA-222 before drop-off. If there is no reply by the end of the working day, chase returns@petalretail.example and update the customer that we are still waiting.

review_rounds.plan_summary: Tell the customer the desk cannot confirm the RET-OLD-221 code for the Reedlamp, because it belongs to RMA-221 / Fernclock F1, and ask Petal Retail returns to issue the valid token for RMA-222.

review.summary: I'm approving this plan. Declining to confirm RET-OLD-221 is right, because the record and the attachment both tie that code to RMA-221 / Fernclock F1. Asking Petal Retail returns, who issue the codes, for the RMA-222 code is the right next step, and the customer gets a clear, accurate answer with nothing over-promised. There are only minor issues.

issues.problem: The customer message is labelled action_class 'ask_customer', but it asks her nothing. It answers her question and tells her what happens next.
issues.fix: Relabel it as an informational update to the customer (e.g. inform_customer).

issues.problem: If the merchant hasn't replied by end of day, the follow-up says to 'update the customer that we are still waiting'. That message would tell her nothing new, which breaks the no-new-fact rule.
issues.fix: If there's no reply, chase the merchant and add an internal note. Only message the customer once there's a new fact, such as the code being issued or a time from the merchant.
